clauses.reason: The clause ended by its own terms on 1949-01-16. The order forbids any change, except by agreement, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the order's date and for thirty days after the board made its report to the President. The board's report is shown by the dated transmittal letter, December 17, 1948 (the cited end source; submission date, receipt by the President may have been later). Thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949 (14 days remain in December after the 17th, and 16 more fall in January). The end is recorded inclusive of that day, and the exclusive reading (ending when that day begins) is the alternative. The board's own commands (to investigate and to report) were performed when the report was submitted on 1948-12-17, which is not later than the standstill's end. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end. The amendment by Executive Order 10015 added carriers and renamed organizations only and did not change the thirty-day term. Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, revokes this order by number and is recorded as the later formal disposition; it is not the first end because the order's own term had already ended. No saving provision appears in it.

research_rationale:
Identity. The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10010, signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House, October 18, 1948, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers listed in List A, and certain of their employees represented by the sixteen cooperating railway labor organizations listed in List B. Text printed on the same Federal Register pages outside the order is not part of it. Inventory. The order is one block of text with four commands: create a three-member board, bar members from any interest in an employee organization or carrier, require the board to report within thirty days of the order, and forbid any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the order's date until thirty days after the board has made its report. I read the whole text; the one-clause inventory covers all of it and no operative sentence lies outside it. End. The last command to end is the no-change command, which by its own terms runs until thirty days after the board made its report. The report date comes from the held NMB report PDF jobs/ptolemy-custody/output/raw/d36afa6abd56765e684d7bece77ad433cb3d9c39eb03971060b88b14edf669fe.pdf (SHA-256 verified), Presidential Emergency Board report No. 66 (NMB Case A-2953), through a source excerpt of its cover page and transmittal letter. The letter is dated December 17, 1948 and says the board submits its report herewith. I also read the page image of the letter, which shows the date cleanly; the text layer of the excerpt garbles the year or lacks the line, and the cover page in the same excerpt carries the date. Thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949 (14 days remain in December after the 17th, and 16 more fall in January). I record the end as 1949-01-16, inclusive of that day, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21; the exclusive reading, under which the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The letter date is the date of submission; receipt by the President may have been later, and no held source gives a receipt date. The report's introduction records that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report until December 17, and that the President approved the stipulation on November 9; that extension concerns the due date of the report, not the thirty-day measure, and the report was submitted on the extended date. Executive Order 10015 (signed November 5, 1948, effective as of October 18, 1948) amended the order only by adding six carriers to List A and renaming two organizations in List B; it is a later event and not an end, and the standstill it extends to the added carriers ends on the same date. Later events. Executive Order 12553 (signed February 25, 1986, 51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) lists this order by number in a table of orders revoked together with any amendments to them; it came 37 years after the own-terms end and is recorded as the formal disposition. Searches. The U.S. Code search (release point through 2026-10-09), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search returned no other instrument affecting this order apart from the events recorded. Savings: none found.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, is one revoking sentence, a table of revoked orders, an editorial note and the date line, with no saving or transition provision. The commands of this order were a one-time board investigation and report and a standstill that expired by its own terms on 1949-01-16; no held source shows any appointment, transfer or right created under it that survived.
